overview: Nov 11-12 was an exceptionally busy day on bpf-next, with 100 patches across 9 series. Alexei Starovoitov landed three interrelated verifier overhauls covering fmod_ret expansion, scalar evolution expression evaluation, and a 29-patch series replacing scalar IDs with scalar-evolution-based register linking. Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi posted the first version of a comprehensive 29-patch series adding automatic resource cleanup on BPF exceptions, while Mike Bazov contributed preemption-safe recursion checking for tracing programs.

patches.title: bpf: Track held resources in hidden stack slots
patches.author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi
patches.summary: This is a core patch from Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi's 29-patch 'Exceptions - Resource Cleanup - Redux' series, which adds automatic cleanup of kernel resources when a BPF program throws an exception via bpf_throw(). The patch introduces hidden stack slots that the verifier uses to track references (map values, kptr handles, locks) held at a throw site, so the runtime can release them on the exception path without requiring the program to do so manually. Earlier patches in the series add arch-specific bpf_throw_unwind() entry hooks and JIT support for capturing callee-saved registers from unwound frames, while later patches extend the mechanism to cover callee-to-caller resource transfers.

patches.title: bpf: Allow fmod_ret on tagged functions and check the return value
patches.author: Alexei Starovoitov
patches.summary: The core feature patch in the v1 fmod_ret expansion series, allowing BPF programs to intercept any kernel function that is automatically tagged by resolve_btfids as returning an error code. Previously the fmod_ret attach type required a hand-curated list of eligible functions; the new tagging approach uses LLVM's MC layer to analyze ELF code and identify functions whose return value is derived from an error on all paths. The verifier is extended to validate the return value that an fmod_ret program installs, preventing programs from inserting non-error codes on the error path.

patches.title: bpf: Remove sync_linked_regs(), refine by scalar evolution only
patches.author: Alexei Starovoitov
patches.summary: A key patch in the 29-part v3 series that replaces the verifier's scalar-ID mechanism with scalar-evolution-based register linking. This patch removes sync_linked_regs(), the function that previously propagated bounds from one register to its scalar-ID partners after a conditional jump, and replaces it with expression evaluation via SCEV. The result is that the verifier can derive tighter bounds for copied loop indices and pointer-arithmetic results without the combinatorial state explosion that scalar IDs caused, while also handling cases that IDs could not, such as sign-extended 32-bit induction variables. Twenty-four companion patches in the series build the SCEV infrastructure, add value-numbering for phi nodes, handle irreducible loops, and finally remove scalar IDs from regsafe() and the state join.

patches.title: bpf: Evaluate the expression of a linked register
patches.author: Alexei Starovoitov
patches.summary: Central patch in the 12-part 'Evaluate scalar evolution expressions in the state after a jump' series, implementing the step that takes a register's symbolic SCEV expression and computes a concrete tightened range after a conditional jump. The verifier can now prove, for example, that a register derived from an induction variable by addition is bounded within the same range as the induction variable itself after the loop test. Companion patches add scalar_intersect(), zero-extension handling, and transfer functions that mirror the verifier's main arithmetic pass so that expressions stay consistent with range narrowing.

patches.title: bpf: Check program recursion per task via bpf_ctx
patches.author: Mike Bazov
patches.summary: Part of Mike Bazov's v2 five-patch series fixing recursion detection for preemptible BPF tracing programs. The existing per-CPU recursion guard breaks when a program running on a preempted CPU is re-entered on the same CPU by a higher-priority context, because both invocations share the same per-CPU slot. This patch threads a per-task recursion counter through bpf_ctx so that the check is task-local and survives preemption. A companion patch extends the fix to syscall tracepoints, and two selftest patches cover trampolines, raw_tp programs, and syscall tracepoints under artificial preemption.

patches.title: bpf: Add struct scalar
patches.author: Alexei Starovoitov
patches.summary: The central patch from the v2 'struct scalar' series, introducing a struct scalar type that bundles the existing cnum (concrete-number range) with a symbolic SCEV expression. Attaching the expression directly to the register avoids re-derivation during backedge analysis and enables the backedge-taken-count feature added in later patches. Prior patches extend cnum with sub, zext32, sext32, and const operations; the subsequent patches add scalar_add() and four further operations, then implement the backedge-taken count that lets the verifier bound loop iterations without conservative fallback.

patches.title: bpf, arm32: build constants inline instead of using a literal pool
patches.author: Ramin Moussavi
patches.summary: A standalone JIT improvement for the 32-bit ARM BPF backend that emits 32-bit immediate constants as a pair of MOV/MOVT instructions rather than loading them from a nearby literal pool. Literal pools require the JIT to manage alignment and pool placement, and can cause cache-line splits when pools and instructions interleave. Inline immediates simplify the code generator and are generally preferable on modern ARM Cortex cores where MOVT has the same latency as a load.
